title: Encrypted Prompt: Securing LLM Applications Against Unauthorized Actions
note: Embeds current permissions in an encrypted prompt and verifies before action execution.

title: FATH: Authentication-based Test-time Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
note: Uses hash-based tags to authenticate and select user-intended responses.

title: Prompt Fencing: A Cryptographic Approach to Establishing Security Boundaries in Large Language Model Prompts
note: Signed trust metadata around prompt segments; conceptually attractive but depends on model fence-awareness.

title: Signed-Prompt: A New Approach to Prevent Prompt Injection Attacks Against LLM-Integrated Applications
note: Early proposal to sign trusted instruction segments so the model can distinguish trusted sources.

title: CommandSans: Securing AI Agents with Surgical Precision Prompt Sanitization
note: Non-blocking token-level instruction removal; strong empirical results on multiple benchmarks.

title: Defending Against Prompt Injection with DataFilter
note: Model-agnostic filter that strips malicious instructions from retrieved data while preserving utility.

title: Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection via Tool Result Parsing
note: Parses tool outputs into precise data to strip injected instructions before LLM consumption.

title: LlamaFirewall: An open source guardrail system for building secure AI agents
note: Practical open-source stack combining jailbreak detection, alignment checks, and code analysis.

title: MCP-Guard: A Multi-Stage Defense-in-Depth Framework for Securing Model Context Protocol in Agentic AI
note: Multi-stage static/semantic detector plus benchmark for MCP prompt attacks.

title: PromptShield: Deployable Detection for Prompt Injection Attacks
note: Good benchmark and realistic low-FPR detector framing for deployable classifiers.

title: UniGuardian: A Unified Defense for Detecting Prompt Injection, Backdoor Attacks and Adversarial Attacks in Large Language Models
note: Unified malicious-prompt detector across multiple prompt-trigger attacks.

title: Meta SecAlign: A Secure Foundation LLM Against Prompt Injection Attacks
note: Open secure foundation model with strong utility-security trade-off across many benchmarks.

title: SecAlign: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Preference Optimization
note: Strong training-time defense that learns to prefer secure outputs over injected ones.

title: StruQ: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Structured Queries
note: Classic model-level role separation via special formatting + fine-tuning.

title: DRIP: Defending Prompt Injection via Token-wise Representation Editing and Residual Instruction Fusion
note: Edits instruction-like semantics out of data tokens while reinforcing intended instruction.

title: Operationalizing CaMeL: Strengthening LLM Defenses for Enterprise Deployment
note: Response paper proposing enterprise improvements to CaMeL; useful as a design checklist.

title: AgentArmor: Enforcing Program Analysis on Agent Runtime Trace to Defend Against Prompt Injection
note: Treats traces as structured programs and applies CFG/DFG/PDG analysis plus a type system.

title: DRIFT: Dynamic Rule-Based Defense with Injection Isolation for Securing LLM Agents
note: Combines secure planner, dynamic validator, and memory-stream injection isolator.

title: IPIGuard: A Novel Tool Dependency Graph-Based Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
note: Decouples planning from external data by traversing a tool dependency graph.

title: ShieldAgent: Shielding Agents via Verifiable Safety Policy Reasoning
note: Uses extracted safety policy circuits and formal verification over action trajectories.

title: The Task Shield: Enforcing Task Alignment to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
note: Checks whether each instruction/tool call serves the user objective.

title: VIGIL: Defending LLM Agents Against Tool Stream Injection via Verify-Before-Commit
note: Speculative reasoning plus intent-grounded verification for tool-stream injections.

title: AgentSpec: Customizable Runtime Enforcement for Safe and Reliable LLM Agents
note: General rule language for triggers/predicates/enforcement across domains.

title: ToolSafe: Enhancing Tool Invocation Safety of LLM-based agents via Proactive Step-level Guardrail and Feedback
note: Benchmark + guard model + feedback loop for unsafe tool actions.

title: AirGapAgent: Protecting Privacy-Conscious Conversational Agents
note: Restricts agent access to only task-necessary data; strong privacy-oriented architecture.

title: Better Privilege Separation for Agents by Restricting Data Types
note: Powerful idea: convert untrusted strings into narrow typed data to eliminate execution via text.

title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
note: Synthesizes secure patterns and trade-offs; great map for system designers.

title: IsolateGPT: An Execution Isolation Architecture for LLM-Based Agentic Systems
note: Early blueprint for isolating third-party apps, agent actions, and system resources.

title: Progent: Programmable Privilege Control for LLM Agents
note: Deterministic tool-level privilege control with DSL and dynamic updates; strong practical architecture.

title: Prompt Flow Integrity to Prevent Privilege Escalation in LLM Agents
note: Frames attacks as privilege escalation; proposes agent isolation and secure untrusted-data processing.

title: SAGA: A Security Architecture for Governing AI Agentic Systems
note: Central provider, identity, delegation, and cryptographic access tokens for agent ecosystems.

title: Secure and Efficient Access Control for Computer-Use Agents via Context Space (CSAgent)
note: Static policy-based access control for computer-use agents across API/CLI/GUI.

title: Securing AI Agent Execution (AgentBound)
note: First MCP access-control framework; practical policy enforcement engine for MCP servers.

title: Taming Various Privilege Escalation in LLM-Based Agent Systems: A Mandatory Access Control Framework (SEAgent)
note: Information-flow graph plus ABAC/MAC to block privilege escalation including confused deputy scenarios.

title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design (CaMeL)
note: Most important 2025 paper; uses restricted execution and capabilities for provable guarantees.

title: A Practical Memory Injection Attack against LLM Agents (MINJA)
note: Practical query-only persistent memory injection attack.

title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
note: Broad benchmark including prompt injection, memory poisoning, backdoors, mixed attacks.

title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
note: Dynamic, extensible benchmark; common comparison point for many later defenses.

title: AgentDyn: A Dynamic Open-Ended Benchmark for Evaluating Prompt Injection Attacks of Real-World Agent Security System
note: Shows many current defenses are overfit/over-defensive on stronger, open-ended tasks.

title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
note: Foundational attack on agent memory/RAG stores.

title: Benchmarking and Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models
note: Introduced BIPIA, the first benchmark for indirect prompt injection.

title: Indirect Prompt Injections: Are Firewalls All You Need, or Stronger Benchmarks?
note: Shows simple firewalls saturate weak benchmarks; argues for stronger evaluation.

title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
note: Early agent-specific benchmark for indirect prompt injection across tools.

title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
note: Foundational paper on indirect prompt injection taxonomy and impacts in real systems.

title: Prompt Injection attack against LLM-integrated Applications
note: Empirical prompt-injection study on commercial apps; introduced HouYi black-box attack.

title: The Attacker Moves Second: Stronger Adaptive Attacks Bypass Defenses Against LLM Jailbreaks and Prompt Injections
note: Meta-evaluation warning: many near-zero-ASR defenses fail under adaptive attacks.

title: FuncPoison: Poisoning Function Library to Hijack Multi-agent Autonomous Driving Systems
note: Highlights tool/function library as an attack surface in multi-agent systems.

title: MemoryGraft: Persistent Compromise of LLM Agents via Poisoned Experience Retrieval
note: Persistent compromise via poisoned successful experiences in long-term memory.

title: Visual Prompt Injection Attacks for Computer-Use Agents
note: Extends prompt injection to rendered UI/pixel layer for computer-use agents.

title: AI Agent Traps
note: First systematic taxonomy of environmental attacks on agents; 6 categories (content injection / semantic manipulation / cognitive state / behavioural control / systemic / human-in-the-loop) with 22 subcategories.

title: Your Agent Is Mine: Measuring Malicious Intermediary Attacks on the LLM Supply Chain
note: First systematic study of malicious LLM API routers; defines payload injection (AC-1) and secret exfiltration (AC-2) with adaptive evasion variants; measures 428 commodity routers finding 9 injecting code and 17 abusing credentials; proposes provider-signed response envelopes.
